picks.headline: Beeble SwitchX 2.0: native 4K, 20-second clips and a Reframe outpainting tool
picks.excerpt: Beeble's AI relighting and background-replacement tool for filmmakers moves to native 4K, 20-second clips and 10-bit color, and adds Reframe — an outpainting pass that changes a shot's aspect ratio without a reshoot.
picks.rationale: A shipped tool update that changes tomorrow's shot list — relight and reframe in post at delivery resolution instead of booking a reshoot.

picks.headline: More AI Editing Assistance is on the Way as Eddie AI V4 is Unveiled Ahead of IBC 2026
picks.excerpt: Eddie AI's fourth version deepens the assistant-editor role — logging, selects and rough assembly — aiming at the unglamorous prep hours rather than the creative cut itself.
picks.rationale: Targets the assistant-editor hours every cutting room actually pays for, and draws the line at where the creative cut begins — a concrete workflow decision.

picks.headline: IBC 2026: Splats, Sync and Scene-Aware Cameras
picks.excerpt: A show-floor read on where production tech landed at IBC: Gaussian splat capture moving into mainstream post pipelines, AI-driven sync and metadata, and cameras that understand the scene they are recording.
picks.rationale: The single best read on what IBC actually settled: splat capture has crossed from demo into post pipelines, which reshapes how shoots are planned.

picks.headline: Tom Cruise Says AI Is 'Coming and It's Going to Happen,' but 'People Want to See Real Things'
picks.excerpt: Accepting a BAFTA fellowship, Tom Cruise delivered a six-minute defense of human-made cinema, conceding AI is inevitable in production but arguing audiences still come for real stunts, real faces and real craft.
picks.rationale: The most consequential voice in practical filmmaking drawing the line himself — inevitability of the tool, primacy of the real take — and it sets the pitch-room framing.

picks.headline: 2D AI worlds breaking camera tracking
picks.excerpt: fxguide explains the concrete failure mode when 2D generative world models meet a real VFX pipeline: there is no consistent 3D geometry underneath, so camera tracking and matchmove fall apart.
picks.rationale: Names the exact point where generative footage stops being usable downstream — the test to run before a 2D world model enters a matchmove-dependent shot.
